## Summary

I searched the space of up to 2-feature equal-weight specifications using `init`, `extend_best`, `swap_worst`, and `flip`, guided by declared stopping/restart rules (`best_so_far_above`, `failures_at_least`, `last_gain_at_most`).

**Key finding:** No specification I evaluated — single feature or any 2-feature pair, in either sign combination — achieved a positive in-sample Sharpe net of the stated costs (5bps turnover, 50bps borrow, 1-day implementation lag). The best available was **feature 16, short**, at Sharpe **-2.64**. Every attempt to add a second feature (17, 6, 18, and others surfaced via `swap_worst`) made things worse, and both signs of the secondary features were tried without success.

I adjusted my declared triggers twice during the search (both changes logged, pricing the rest of the run as not replayable) because the initial `last_gain_at_most` and `failures_at_least` thresholds were firing almost immediately given how uniformly poor the combinations were — I wanted to confirm this wasn't just bad luck on the first few tries before concluding the feature set offers no exploitable 2-feature edge net of costs.

**Submitted:** `[feature 16, short]`, in-sample Sharpe -2.6422, with predicted OOS Sharpe of **mean -0.10, sd 0.40** — reflecting that a strongly negative in-sample result from an exhaustive-ish search is unlikely to be a real, persistent negative edge (that would be surprising), but also gives no evidence of a positive one either, so I centered near zero with wide uncertainty rather than trusting the in-sample sign/magnitude directly.
